name: Moving Rigid Body Free Surface Validation
goal: A rigorous survey of what validates a rigid body moving through free-surface water, to define falsifiable validation targets for a moving road vehicle in floodwater. Rank by transferability: experimental hydrodynamics with measured reference data first, VOF/finite-volume CFD validated against those experiments second, MPM only where relevant work exists. DO NOT TREAT SPH AS A CO-EQUAL SOURCE; include it only when it points to an independently useful experimental dataset, tagged dataset-only, and never to set acceptable error bands or resolution guidance. Also investigate added mass and unsteady drag for a bluff body accelerating near a free surface. Determine whether the commonly cited current-velocity limit of 1.5 m/s has an experimental basis or is a doctrinal rule of thumb. Keep still-water depth limits separate from depth-velocity products.
summary:
The most transferable validation targets are measured vehicle forces and stability thresholds from full-scale or scale-model flood experiments [Smi19, Kra16, Sha20], with VOF/RANS vehicle-wading studies giving the clearest method-specific comparison [Xin21b, Alq22]; NO VALIDATED VEHICLE-FORDING MPM CHAIN IS IDENTIFIED.

EXPERIMENTAL ANCHORS: traction, buoyancy, drag and incipient motion measured in [Smi19], [Arr15], [Shu11], [Xia13b], [Alq21]; [Sha20] reports R2 = 0.85. [Kra16] proposes total-head criteria of 0.3 m for passenger cars and 0.6 m for emergency vehicles, and STILL-WATER DEPTH LIMITS MUST NOT BE CONFLATED WITH DEPTH-VELOCITY PRODUCTS.
CFD VALIDATION: [Xin21b] compares rotating-wheel VOF/RANS with road tests; [Alq22] reports simulated critical depth 0.38 m and minimum depth x velocity 0.39 m2/s against prior experiments. THESE ARE CASE-SPECIFIC AGREEMENTS, NOT UNIVERSAL TOLERANCES.
CANONICAL TRANSFERABLE HYDRODYNAMICS: accelerating-plate drag and free-surface effects in [Gri19] and [Wau69]; near-surface added mass and damping in [Chu77]; dam-break obstacle pressures with openly supplied measurements and video in [Kam19]; planing-hull force data in [Rus07]; baffled-tank loads with grid-refinement evidence in [Sam02]. [Kra21b] IS AN UNUSUALLY PRECISE PUBLIC BENCHMARK, ABOUT 0.3 PERCENT EXPERIMENTAL UNCERTAINTY.
[Azh23] IS SPH AND DATASET-ONLY: useful for its laboratory vehicle measurements, NOT for SPH error bands or acceptance standards.

The records DO NOT establish an experimental basis for the 1.5 m/s rule, do not identify a validated reconstruction-to-simulation-to-fording pipeline, and do not resolve DOI identifiers.
